subject.name: Advanced Mathematics
subject.description: Official Grade 12 Advanced Mathematics competency records.

standards.text: The learners can analyze and model real-life situations using linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. They construct, evaluate, and verify these algebraically and graphically, apply function transformations using appropriate technology to represent and interpret solutions, and explain key function behaviors and limitations. The learners can also distinguish among these function types using data, graphs, and context, and evaluate the suitability and reasonableness of models in business, science, and everyday applications. They communicate conclusions using graphs, tables, equations, and written explanations to support sound decision-making. The learners can also model real-life phenomena using angle and radian measures, arc length, area of a sector, and trigonometric functions. They can present scenario analyses and clearly communicate their reasoning through visual and algebraic representations demonstrating how these concepts support problem-solving and informed decision-making in science, technology, and engineering.

The learners can use their understanding of trigonometric concepts to analyze, represent, and solve mathematical and real-life situations. They can apply key trigonometric formulas to simplify expressions, justify steps, and construct proofs, and evaluate and interpret trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions using appropriate strategies. The learners communicate ideas through graphs, equations, tables, and explanations, showing ease in shifting between different representations. When solving contextual problems, they can apply inverse trigonometric functions to generate reasonable solutions and explain their significance. *To extend their mathematical understanding, the learners can use the polar coordinate system to describe and analyze relationships that are not effectively represented in rectangular coordinates. They can locate and convert points, identify and sketch polar curves, and use these tools to model real-world situations accurately. The learners can integrate their understanding of trigonometric identities, inverse functions, and coordinate systems to build meaningful models, explain reasoning effectively, and make informed decisions, demonstrating how abstract mathematical ideas connect to practical applications in science, technology, engineering, and everyday problem-solving.

competencies.text: differentiate between linear, quadratic, and exponential models based on data patterns or graphs.
interpret linear models in real-life contexts such as cost analysis, revenue prediction, or population growth.
interpret quadratic models in real-life contexts involving area, projectile motion, or optimization.
interpret exponential models in real-life contexts such as compound interest, population growth, or decay.
evaluate the appropriateness, reasonableness, and limitations of using linear, quadratic, or exponential models in a given real-life context.
identify an angle by describing its initial and terminal sides and its direction of rotation (clockwise or counterclockwise).
sketch angles in standard position.
convert radian measures to degree measures and vice versa.
use radian measure to find the arc length and the area of a sector.
solve problems involving radian measure, arc length, and area of a sector.
illustrate the different trigonometric functions in relation to the unit circle.
use reference angles to find values of trigonometric functions.
determine the domain and range of the different trigonometric functions.
graph the six trigonometric functions using features such as amplitude, period, phase shift, and asymptotes.
express trigonometric functions of acute angles as functions of the complement of the angle, using cofunction identities.
simplify trigonometric expressions by using Pythagorean identities.
solve problems involving trigonometric functions including periodic phenomena.
apply sum and difference formulas for trigonometric functions to simplify expressions.
apply double-angle and half-angle formulas to find exact values or simplify trigonometric expressions.
prove trigonometric identities by applying the appropriate formulas.
solve problems involving trigonometric identities.
illustrate the domain and range of the inverse trigonometric functions.
graph inverse trigonometric functions.
evaluate inverse trigonometric expressions.
solve problems involving inverse trigonometric functions.
illustrate the polar coordinate system.
locate points in the polar coordinate system.
convert coordinates from rectangular to polar systems and vice versa.
identify polar curves from their equations.
sketch the graphs of polar equations.
solve problems involving the polar coordinate system.
